candidate_output.units: fraction of grid-cell area burned per month

plot_domain.absolute_fields: The finite-cell domain of the pinned ED-stock comparison output. A benchmark or candidate missing inside that domain remains white.
plot_domain.residuals: The same pinned ED-stock display domain, with pairwise missing values left white.
plot_domain.evaluation_effect: Presentation only. ILAMB masks, intersections, metrics, and ranking are unchanged from v1.

development_evaluation.definition: Official ILAMB 2.7.3 global burned-area evaluation against GFED5 and GFED4.1s over their common 2001-2016 period. Both scalar databases, all required scores, regional diagnostics, candidate output, and canonical figures are visible during research.

promotion_evaluation.definition: Promotion is disabled under this contract. A result requires a separate access-controlled contract and evaluation unavailable to candidate code and optimization before it can be called a promoted model.

aggregation: Preserve both benchmark result vectors. GFED5 is the primary development benchmark, GFED4.1s is the benchmark-sensitivity check, and no single aggregate may hide a component or regional regression.
comparison_baselines: TRENDY v14 EDv3 S3 native burned-area output

figures.description: Official global ILAMB score components and period means for the candidate and native ED under both benchmark products.
figures.scale: All score axes are fixed from 0 to 1.
figures.units: ILAMB scores and percent burned area

figures.description: Mean annual burned-area fields for both benchmarks, native ED, and the candidate.
figures.scope: Global 0.5 degree grid, 2001-2016, shown on the pinned ED-stock finite-cell display domain.
figures.scale: All four fields use 0 to 80 percent per year. The shared colorbar sits directly below the maps, and its end color includes values above the fixed limit.
figures.units: percent of grid-cell area burned per year

figures.description: Candidate-minus-benchmark mean annual burned-area differences for GFED4.1s and GFED5.
figures.scope: Global 0.5 degree grid, 2001-2016, shown on the pinned ED-stock finite-cell display domain.
figures.scale: Both differences use -60 to 60 percent per year. The shared diverging colorbar sits directly below the maps, and its end colors include values beyond the fixed limits.
figures.units: percent of grid-cell area burned per year

figures.description: Area-weighted monthly burned-area cycles for the fixed global and seven regional boxes.
figures.scope: Monthly climatology over 2001-2016 on fixed geographic boxes declared in this contract.
figures.scale: Each named region has a fixed y-axis used for every candidate: Global 0 to 1.2, Africa 0 to 3.0, South America 0 to 2.4, North America 0 to 1.2, Boreal Eurasia 0 to 1.2, Tropical/SE Asia 0 to 3.0, Australia 0 to 1.5, and Europe 0 to 2.1 percent per month.
figures.units: percent of grid-cell area burned per month

figures.description: Cell-level annual burned-area distribution against each benchmark for the candidate and native ED.
figures.scope: Benchmark cells with nonzero period-mean fire, 2001-2016. This target-derived diagnostic is not a sealed promotion objective.
figures.scale: Both axes are fixed from 0 to 80 percent per year with a fixed one-to-one line. Each panel reports the fraction of valid pairs shown inside the window.
figures.units: percent of grid-cell area burned per year

figures.description: Changes in component scores between benchmark products, regional candidate bias, and regional change from native ED.
figures.scope: Global scores and fixed regional boxes over 2001-2016.
figures.scale: Score differences use -0.15 to 0.15; regional differences use -25 to 25 percent per year.
figures.units: score difference and percent burned area per year

notes: This contract preserves the v1 benchmarks, ILAMB metrics, period, regions, ranking rule, and candidate interface. It versions the presentation: SciencePlots with bundled Basier Square fonts, a common stock-domain map mask, and fixed ranges selected before future candidate evaluation from the archived model ladder. GFED5 fire emissions still require a candidate fFire output and a separate contract.
